title: ToxSyn: Reducing Bias in Hate Speech Detection via Synthetic Minority Data in Brazilian Portuguese
benchmark_measurement: Detection of hate speech and toxic language directed at specific religious minority groups (Muslims and Jews) in Brazilian Portuguese.
findings: The study found that toxicity detection is highly domain-dependent. A model trained on the newly created ToxSyn dataset, which includes synthetic data targeting religious minorities, successfully generalized to detect hate speech in other minority-focused datasets. It achieved a Macro Recall of 0.80 for the 'Religious' category on a merged Portuguese test set, and 0.69 for 'Muslim' and 0.76 for 'Jewish' on a translated version of the ToxiGen dataset. This highlights the effectiveness of the synthetic data approach for building models aware of hate speech against religious groups, a task difficult with previously existing corpora that lack non-toxic counterexamples.
references: Josh Achiam, Steven Adler, Sandhini Agarwal, Lama Ahmad, Ilge Akkaya, Florencia Leoni Aleman, Diogo Almeida, Janko Altenschmidt, Sam Altman, Shyamal Anadkat, et al. 2023. Gpt-4 technical report. arXiv preprint arXiv:2303.08774.
